tell: 'Congrats on the promotion — you earned it.' is generic filler with no voice markers at all — no 'y'all', 'folks', exclamation-stacking, or personal anecdote anywhere in his real posts, even short ones.

'Most experiential agencies are sitting on a platform problem, and nobody wants to admit it.' is a textbook LinkedIn-thought-leader hook — too rhetorically tight and depersonalized versus his rambling, anecdote-first voice.
Generic 'you earned it' with no named person, company, or concrete detail — every reference post, even short ones like REF6, anchors itself in a specific fact.
Copies REF7's rhetorical skeleton almost beat-for-beat (claim → 'Why?' → 'Because...' → reframe → half-joking business idea → single emoji), reading like template reuse rather than organic variation.
generic and flat — 'you earned it. 🎉' has none of his signature markers ('folks', 'y'all', 'freaking', stacked emoji, personal detail)

the crafted aphorism 'That's backwards.' and clipped 'Half joking. Mostly not.' read as polished thought-leader rhythm — missing the 'folks'/exclamation-heavy warmth of his genuinely similar hybrid-work post
